overview: Pendour Cove is a tiny, wild cove about a mile north-west of Zennor, just west of Zennor Head, on the rugged north coast of the West Penwith moors. It’s not a beach for a lazy day with all the trimmings, but it’s a magical spot to reach on foot.

It’s the setting for a much-loved Cornish legend, the Mermaid of Zennor. The story goes that a mermaid fell for a local man with a beautiful singing voice and lured him into the sea, and that on a fine summer evening you might still hear him singing from the cove.

expect.title: The legend
expect.text: Sit above the cove on a fine summer evening and, the story says, you might hear the drowned singer.

expect.title: Wild coast
expect.text: Rugged cliffs and moorland all around, with the coast path above.

goodToKnow.label: Facilities
goodToKnow.text: There are no facilities, so take everything you need.

goodToKnow.label: Getting there
goodToKnow.text: On foot from Zennor along the coast path.

week.text: Part of a walking day around Zennor rather than a beach day. Combine it with the village and its church, and the ancient sites on the moors behind.

pairWith.why: the village and its mermaid legend
an Iron Age village on the moor

tips: Wear walking boots: it’s a rough path down to the cove.
